In condition (가), sqrt(a) in the denominator forces a>0, and both radical arguments require bc>=0; for a>0 these conditions make the two sides equal. Condition (나) is equivalent to b>=c; because the cards are distinct, b>c. rows.reasoning: Let h=g-x and D=x^2g-8. Polynomial division says f^2+7h^2=QD and deg(-7h^2)<deg(D). Since f has degree 2 and real leading coefficient 2, the sum of squares has degree max(4,2deg(h)); comparing degrees shows deg(h)<=1 (if deg(h)>=2 then the remainder degree is at least deg(D)). The constant-g case is impossible because the remainder (g-x)^2 has degree 2 while D has degree at most 2. Hence g=ux+v with u nonzero, D has degree 3, and Q has degree 1. Since (x-1)(x-2) divides gQ, the linear factors g and Q must account for the two distinct roots one each. The alternative g(2)=0, Q(1)=0 violates |g(1)|<|g(2)|, so g(1)=0 and Q(2)=0. Thus g=u(x-1), Q=A(x-2); leading terms give A=4/u. Writing f=2x^2+px+q and comparing coefficients in f^2+7u^2(x-1)^2=(4/u)(x-2)(ux^3-ux^2-8) yields p=-3, q=-(1+7u^2)/4, 7u^3-3u-64=0, and q^2+7u^2=64/u. Substituting the cubic into the constant equation gives 7u^2+u+5=0, whose discriminant is 1-140<0. Therefore no real u exists, so no real f,g satisfy the stated conditions and the requested maximum does not exist.
